title: Yesterday: the simple past
intro: Good news: the Persian past tense is the most regular thing in the language. Every verb has a past stem, the past stem is simply the infinitive without -an, and the endings are ones you already know. In this lesson you learn to say what you did yesterday, where you were and what you didn't do – and to ask the question every Iranian asks after a weekend: خوش گذشت؟
goals: say what you did with the simple past: رفتم، خوردم، دیدم
say where you were with the past of بودن: بودم
say what you didn't do: نرفتم، نبودم
use past time words: دیروز، پریروز، دیشب، هفته‌ی پیش، دو روز پیش

sections.title: What did you do on Friday?
sections.context: Saturday morning, the first day of the Iranian working week. Sara meets Amir at the office.

lines.en: Hi Amir! Where were you yesterday?

lines.fa: سلام! دیروز جمعه بود. با دوستانم به دربند رفتم.
lines.r: salām! diruz jom'e bud. bā dustān-am be Darband raftam.
lines.en: Hi! Yesterday was Friday. I went to Darband with my friends.
lines.col: سلام! دیروز جمعه بود. با دوستام رفتم دربند.
lines.colR: salām! diruz jom'e bud. bā dust-ām raftam Darband.

lines.en: How nice! Did you go up the mountain?

lines.fa: بله، صبح زود رفتیم و تا ظهر راه رفتیم.
lines.r: bale, sobh-e zud raftim o tā zohr rāh raftim.
lines.en: Yes, we went early in the morning and walked until noon.
lines.col: آره، صبح زود رفتیم و تا ظهر راه رفتیم.
lines.colR: āre, sobh-e zud raftim o tā zohr rāh raftim.

lines.en: What did you have for lunch?

lines.fa: در یک رستوران کوچک کباب و دوغ خوردیم. خیلی خوشمزه بود!
lines.r: dar yek resturān-e kuchak kabāb o dugh khordim. kheyli khoshmaze bud!
lines.en: We had kebab and doogh in a small restaurant. It was delicious!
lines.col: تو یه رستوران کوچیک کباب و دوغ خوردیم. خیلی خوشمزه بود!
lines.colR: tu ye resturān-e kuchik kabāb o dugh khordim. kheyli khoshmaze bud!

lines.fa: من هیچ جا نرفتم. خانه بودم و درس خواندم.
lines.r: man hich jā na-raftam. khāne budam o dars khāndam.
lines.en: I didn't go anywhere. I was at home and studied.
lines.col: من هیچ جا نرفتم. خونه بودم و درس خوندم.
lines.colR: man hich jā na-raftam. khune budam o dars khundam.

lines.en: You studied the day before yesterday too!

lines.fa: بله، امتحان دارم. اما شب با خانواده‌ام شام خوردیم و فیلم دیدیم.
lines.r: bale, emtehān dāram. ammā shab bā khānevāde-am shām khordim o film didim.
lines.en: Yes, I have an exam. But in the evening I had dinner with my family and we watched a film.
lines.col: آره، امتحان دارم. ولی شب با خانواده‌م شام خوردیم و فیلم دیدیم.
lines.colR: āre, emtehān dāram. vali shab bā khānevāde-m shām khordim o film didim.

lines.en: Did you have a good time?

lines.fa: بد نبود. اما دفعه‌ی بعد من هم با شما به کوه می‌آیم!
lines.r: bad na-bud. ammā daf'e-ye ba'd man ham bā shomā be kuh mi-āyam!
lines.en: It wasn't bad. But next time I'm coming to the mountains with you!
lines.col: بد نبود. ولی دفعه‌ی بعد منم باهاتون میام کوه!
lines.colR: bad na-bud. vali daf'e-ye ba'd man-am bā-hātun miyām kuh!

sections.title: The easiest tense in Persian
sections.md:
Every Persian verb has two stems. The present stem (rav- in [[می‌روم|mi-ravam]]) can be irregular, but the **past stem** never is: it is the infinitive without **-an**. [[رفتن|raftan|to go]] → [[رفت|raft]], [[خوردن|khordan|to eat]] → [[خورد|khord]], [[دیدن|didan|to see]] → [[دید|did]].

To make the simple past, add the person endings you know from *to be* in lesson 1 – **-am, -i, -im, -id, -and** – with one exception: *he / she* has no ending at all. [[رفتم|raftam|I went]], [[رفتی|rafti|you went]], [[رفت|raft|he / she went]]. There is no mi- and no be-.

Say it with the stress on the **stem**, not on the ending: *RAF-tam, KHOR-dim, ā-MA-dand*. And to say what you did **not** do, put **na-** in front – it takes the stress: *NA-raftam*, [[نرفتم|na-raftam|I didn't go]].

ex.fa: دو روز پیش به تهران آمدم.
ex.r: do ruz pish be Tehrān āmadam.
ex.en: I came to Tehran two days ago.

items.note: past stem آمد āmad; spoken umad-
past: بودم budam, بودی budi, بود bud…
past stem خواند khānd; spoken khund-

ex.en: On Friday we went to the mountains.

items.note: literally 'it passed pleasantly'; as a question: Did you have a good time?

sections.title: The simple past: رفتم، خوردم، دیدم
sections.md:
Past stem + ending. That is all, for every verb in the language:

- [[آمدن|āmadan]] → [[آمدم|āmadam|I came]]
- [[کردن|kardan]] → [[کردم|kardam|I did]], so [[کار کردم|kār kardam|I worked]]
- [[گفتن|goftan]] → [[گفتم|goftam|I said]]
- [[خریدن|kharidan]] → [[خریدم|kharidam|I bought]]
- [[شدن|shodan]] → [[شدم|shodam|I became]]

The subject pronoun is usually dropped, because the ending already says who did it: [[رفتیم|raftim]] can only mean *we went*. In speech **-id** becomes **-in** and **-and** becomes **-an**: *raftin, raftan*.

examples.en: Yesterday I went to the bazaar.
examples.note: in speech the place often comes after the verb, without be

examples.en: Last year they went to Isfahan.

examples.fa: تام هفته‌ی پیش یک فرش خرید.
examples.r: Tām hafte-ye pish yek farsh kharid.
examples.en: Tom bought a carpet last week.

sections.title: I was, I wasn't, I didn't: بودم، نبودم، نرفتم
sections.md:
The past of [[بودن|budan|to be]] follows the same pattern: [[بودم|budam|I was]], [[بودی|budi|you were]], [[بود|bud|he / she / it was]]. It is used for where you were and what something was like: [[خسته بودم|khaste budam|I was tired]], [[هوا سرد بود|havā sard bud|it was cold]].

For the negative, join **na-** to the front of any past verb: [[نبودم|na-budam|I wasn't]], [[نخوردم|na-khordam|I didn't eat]]. In a compound verb na- goes on the verb part: [[کار نکردم|kār na-kardam|I didn't work]]. Before the long **ā** of [[آمدن|āmadan]], na- becomes **nay-**: [[نیامدم|na-yāmadam|I didn't come]].

examples.fa: هوا سرد بود و ما بیرون نرفتیم.
examples.r: havā sard bud o mā birun na-raftim.
examples.en: It was cold and we didn't go out.
I didn't have dinner last night.
Reza didn't come to the party.

sections.title: When? Words for the past
sections.md:
Time words usually come first in the sentence, or right after the subject. [[پیش|pish|ago]] comes **after** the amount of time, the opposite of English: [[دو روز پیش|do ruz pish|two days ago]], [[سه سال پیش|se sāl pish|three years ago]].

For *last week, last month* use [[پیش|pish]] with an ezafe: [[هفته‌ی پیش|hafte-ye pish]], [[ماه پیش|māh-e pish]]. *Last year* has its own word, [[پارسال|pārsāl]]. To ask *when?*, use [[کی؟|key?]]

examples.fa: کی به تهران آمدی؟ سه ماه پیش.
examples.r: key be Tehrān āmadi? se māh pish.
examples.en: When did you come to Tehran? Three months ago.
examples.col: کی اومدی تهران؟ سه ماه پیش.
examples.colR: key umadi Tehrān? se māh pish.

examples.en: Yesterday morning I bought sangak bread.
The day before yesterday was my mother's birthday.

examples.fa: او یک ساعت پیش به من زنگ زد.
examples.r: u yek sā'at pish be man zang zad.
examples.en: He rang me an hour ago.

sections.title: A day in Isfahan
sections.intro: Leila and Dariush took a trip last week. Every verb in the story is in the simple past.

sentences.fa: هفته‌ی پیش لیلا و داریوش به اصفهان رفتند.
sentences.r: hafte-ye pish Leylā o Dāriush be Esfahān raftand.
sentences.en: Last week Leila and Dariush went to Isfahan.

sentences.fa: آن‌ها با قطار رفتند و ساعت نه صبح رسیدند.
sentences.r: ān-hā bā ghatār raftand o sā'at-e noh-e sobh residand.
sentences.en: They went by train and arrived at nine in the morning.

sentences.fa: اول به میدان نقش جهان رفتند.
sentences.r: avval be meydān-e Naghsh-e Jahān raftand.
sentences.en: First they went to Naqsh-e Jahan Square.

sentences.fa: ظهر در یک رستوران سنتی بریانی خوردند.
sentences.r: zohr dar yek resturān-e sonnati beryāni khordand.
sentences.en: At noon they ate beryani, Isfahan's famous lamb dish, in a traditional restaurant.
In the late afternoon they walked on Si-o-se Pol, the bridge of thirty-three arches.

sentences.fa: شب خسته بودند، اما خیلی خوش گذشت.
sentences.r: shab khaste budand, ammā kheyli khosh gozasht.
sentences.en: In the evening they were tired, but they had a great time.
Leila said: "Isfahan is half the world!"

sections.title: Friday: the Iranian weekend
sections.md:
In Iran the week starts on [[شنبه|shanbe|Saturday]] and the day off is [[جمعه|jom'e|Friday]]; for many people Thursday afternoon is free too. So the Monday-morning question of other countries is asked on Saturday: [[جمعه چه کار کردی؟|jom'e che kār kardi?|What did you do on Friday?]]

A classic Tehran Friday starts early in the mountains. At dawn thousands of people walk up the valley of [[دربند|Darband]] or the slopes of Tochal, stop for tea, dates and a breakfast of [[عدسی|adasi|lentil soup]] at a café by the stream, and are back down before the sun gets hot. Lunch is a long family meal at the grandparents' – often [[آبگوشت|ābgusht]] – and the evening is for visits and television.

If you missed a good outing, your friends will tell you [[جای شما خالی بود!|jā-ye shomā khāli bud!|your place was empty]] – *we missed you*. It is the polite reply to *khosh gozasht?* as well.

sections.title: Tips
items: The past stem is the infinitive minus **-an** – always. Learn every new verb by its infinitive and you get its past for free.

Stress the stem, not the ending: *RAF-tam, KHOR-dim, ā-MA-dand* – the endings are unstressed. With **na-** the stress moves to the front: *NA-raftam*. (At A2 you will see why this matters: *raf-TAM*, stressed at the end, is spoken Persian for 'I have gone'.)
**na-** is written joined to the verb: نرفتم، نخوردم، نبودم. Before آ it becomes **nay-**: نیامدم *na-yāmadam*, spoken *nayumadam*.
In speech **-id** becomes **-in** and **-and** becomes **-an**: *raftin, raftan*. Some stems change too: *āmad-* → *umad-*, *khānd-* → *khund-*.
After a trip or a party everyone asks **khosh gozasht?** The happy answer is *kheyli khosh gozasht!* – and if your friend wasn't there, add *jā-ye shomā khāli!*

items.explain: Past stem raft + -am (I): raftam. raft alone means 'he / she went'.

items.q: Which word means 'the day before yesterday'?
items.explain: pariruz; diruz is yesterday and pārsāl last year.
na- + khordam. نمی‌خوردم is the negative past continuous ('I wasn't eating'), which comes at A2.
bud + -and (they): budand. hastand is the present 'they are'.
pish (ago) comes after the amount of time: do ruz pish. do ruz ba'd is 'two days later'.

items.en: Last week we went to Shiraz.
Yesterday I went to the bazaar.
I didn't have dinner last night.
Last year they went to Isfahan.
Did you have a good time?
